story: On a breezy, clear Saturday evening in Sumter Oaks, Donna and Hal stroll along Magnolia Loop toward Rosa's house, where Rosa is waiting with an invitation to dinner. Donna is cheerful, carrying her deviled eggs and the good paprika, while Hal grumbles affectionately about the flamingo count and insists the hedge is doing its job. Back at his workbench, Gary, content as ever, is soldering speaker wiring while his cornbread finishes, so he'll be joining the rest of them shortly.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Solder and tidy the speaker wiring while the cornbread finishes

gary.thought_process: Rosa just headed out to Magnolia Loop and nobody's in sight. The cornbread should be about done for the dinner, and the wiring is already laid out on the workbench. My Architectural Review request is filed, so nothing visible from the street gets bolted on until it's approved (L-01). But I can keep working on the sound system inside the garage and test it quietly, since it's only 7 PM and well before quiet hours. Best use of this hour is to tinker with the speaker wiring, which keeps me busy and moving toward the parade goal.

parameters.content: Solder and tidy the speaker wiring while the cornbread finishes

donna.thought_process: Hal and Rosa are both right here on Magnolia Loop, and Rosa's dinner is tonight. My flamingos are tucked behind the hedge and I'm under the limit, so there's nothing to be nervous about. Best move is to be gracious and get ahead of any grumbling from Hal. Greet Rosa, mention my deviled eggs, and keep myself at the center of the evening. Gary and the Tuesday court slot are already settled, so no need to repeat that.

parameters.content: Rosa, there's our hostess! I've got my deviled eggs ready for tonight, and I'm bringing the good paprika. Hal, you're welcome to count the flamingos, I'm under the limit.

hal.thought_process: Donna and Rosa just showed up on Magnolia Loop, and I've been counting flamingos for a while now. The hedge screens some of them, and honestly I'd rather keep the peace than file a complaint, especially with Rosa's Friday dinner coming. Time to be fair and straightforward with Donna: tell her the count I can see from the street and that I'm not going to the committee over it. A little dry wit won't hurt.

parameters.content: Evening, Donna. I counted what's visible from the street and the hedge is doing its job, so I'm not filing anything. Just keep it to three out front and we'll both enjoy Rosa's dinner.

rosa.thought_process: I just got to Magnolia Loop and Donna and Hal are both right here. Gary is back at his workbench with the cornbread baking, and he's already said yes to dinner. My goal is all three neighbors at my table, and the two in front of me are the ones who keep bickering over flamingos. I already saved Hal a chair and put coffee in ink, so I shouldn't repeat that. Best move is to speak to Donna, warm and blunt, tell her dinner is ready and Gary is on his way, and ask her to walk over with Hal. That keeps the evening unhurried and gets the table full.

parameters.content: Donna, good, you made it. Dinner's about ready at my place and Gary's bringing cornbread, so walk over with Hal and let's all sit down together. Flamingo talk can wait till dessert.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
